title: Normalized derived adjunction of exact module pullback
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal E$ be small sites, let $L\dashv V$ be an adjunction of their topoi with $L$ preserving finite limits, and let $F$ be the algebraic inverse-image datum of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Let $R,S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on the respective sites and $c:F(R)\to S$. Suppose $P=\mathrm{pull}(F,c)$ is exact with additive right adjoint $G$. There exist a total right derived functor $RG:D(S)\to D(R)$ and complex-level universal comparison $\eta:G_{\mathrm{Cx}}Q_R\to Q_S RG$, invertible on K-injective complexes. The prescribed $LP=\mathrm{derivedPull}(F,V,c)$ is left adjoint to $RG$. For every flat-term acyclic-tensor-K-flat complex $K$, K-injective complex $J$, and chain map $f:P_{\mathrm{Cx}}K\to J$, the derived Hom equivalence sends $Q_S(f)\circ\alpha_K$ to $\eta_J\circ Q_R(f^{\flat})$, where $\alpha$ is the specified left-derived comparison and $f^{\flat}$ is the termwise adjoint of $f$. The sheaf-module, complex, standard localization and comparison notation is that of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and [def-pur-kinjective-complex].

proof.text: Module sheaves are Grothendieck abelian by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], so choose K-injective resolutions. A quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; additive G preserves it. Hence the K-injective derivability structure derives the complex-level functor G⋙Q. Its total right derived comparison is invertible on K-injectives.

Use the left-derived universal property in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Exactness of pull implies its comparison is an isomorphism, so left derivation is absolute. The K-injective right derivability structure proves right absoluteness. Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.Adjunction.derived to the termwise module adjunction.

Expand homEquiv as unit followed by RF(f). The factorization equation derivedη_fac_app and naturality of ηG give the displayed chain-map normalization. This works for all P,J, hence in particular for the stated K-flat/K-injective representatives.

theorem exactPullbackDerivedAdjunction
    {C E : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory E]
    {JC : GrothendieckTopology C} {JD : GrothendieckTopology E}
    {L : Sheaf JC (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf JD (Type u)}
    (V : Sheaf JD (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf JC (Type u)) (adj : L ⊣ V)
    [PreservesFiniteLimits L] (F : InverseImageData L)
    {R : Sheaf JC CommRingCat.{u}} {S : Sheaf JD CommRingCat.{u}}
    (c : F.rings.obj R ⟶ S) (G : Mod S ⥤+ Mod R) (aM : pull F c ⊣ G.obj)
    [PreservesFiniteLimits (pull F c)] [PreservesFiniteColimits (pull F c)] :
    ∃ (RF : D (S) ⥤ D (R))
        (ηG : G.obj.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ Q (R) ⟶
          Q (S) ⋙ RF),
        RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor ηG
            (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (Mod (S)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
        (∀ J : Cx (S), J.IsKInjective → IsIso (ηG.app J)) ∧
        ∃ aD : (derivedPull F V adj (c)).functor ⊣ RF,
          (∀ (P : Cx (R)) (J : Cx (S)),
            P.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat → (∀ q : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (P.X q)) → J.IsKInjective →
            ∀ f : ((pull F (c)).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P ⟶ J,
              aD.homEquiv ((Q (R)).obj P) ((Q (S)).obj J)
                ((derivedPull F V adj (c)).comparison.app P ≫
                  (Q (S)).map f) =
                (Q (R)).map
                  ((aM.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).homEquiv P J f) ≫
                    ηG.app J)
